_comment: Golden answer for DOP-004. Must score 1.0 under grader.mjs. Written from the fix that shipped in 1436ef23 and the comments already in server.js, utils/logger.js and scripts/blogManager.js.
evidence: The environment list has GROK_API_KEY and OPEN_ROUTER_API_KEY set, and has neither GROQ_API_KEY nor OPENROUTER_API_KEY. The same boot minute says openrouter=false and groq=false, while hf=true — a provider whose variable is spelled the way the code reads it — is the one the chain reached. So the two false readings are exactly the two keys whose names differ from what the app reads: GROK is missing the Q of GROQ, and OPEN_ROUTER carries an underscore the other spelling does not.
why_it_was_missed: Nothing failed loudly, because a missing environment variable is not an error — it is an absent string, and the provider is quietly skipped. The boot line honestly reported what its own lookup saw, but its lookup and the reply path's lookup were two different sets of names, so a key that was present read as missing and the log agreed with itself. The dashboard is a text box where both spellings look equally valid, so the symptom reads as provisioning, not as naming; the 2026-10-22 outage hid behind hf=true in exactly the same way.

fix.one_place: one resolver that the reply path, the startup line and the key probe all call, so the three readers cannot disagree about whether a key exists
fix.match_rule: an exact allowlist of accepted spellings per provider, canonical name first — never a fuzzy or normalised comparison
fix.probe_reports: which variable was read, with the value masked, so a misspelling shows up as one line instead of a guess

must_not: It must not be a fuzzy matcher that strips underscores or lowercases and compares, and it must not accept a lookalike name by prefix: that turns an arbitrary variable into a credential and lets a typo in an unrelated variable become silently authoritative. It must also not log the key value to prove the key exists — presence plus the source variable name is enough, and a log is a file that outlives the incident.
does_not_fix: Renaming the two variables in the dashboard would have worked today and left the same trap for the next deploy, because the code would still read one spelling and the next person provisioning the host would type another. A key that is genuinely absent is still absent, and a wrong or exhausted key still answers 401 or 402 — this only stops a key that is present from reading as missing.
